solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

flags: minor: answer cue - D is the only hedged choice ('sometimes'); A is an absolute that the passage directly rejects, B contradicts para 5, C is a narrow detail, so the distractors are weak
minor: overlaps with R030-07 (both turn on 'collapse is one possible ending, not the only one'); R030-01's key partly gives away R030-07
R030-01.notes: Passage moves from Hardin's theory to Ostrom's field evidence that collapse is not inevitable. C is a true detail but not the main idea.

flags: minor: pure lookup - stem quotes the passage sentence almost word for word and A paraphrases its ending
minor: B is Ostrom's view, a reasonable trap for skimmers, but C and D would draw almost no one

minor: factual nuance - Hardin's 1968 essay mainly called for 'mutual coercion, mutually agreed upon' and discussed private property and government regulation; the passage's 'private property or government control' summary is the standard reading and acceptable
R030-02.notes: Para 1 last sentence: divided into private property or placed under government control.

R030-03.notes: Para 2: argument spread quickly and was treated 'less as a hypothesis to be tested than as a law.' A misreads 'seemed to explain'; C belongs to para 3; D wrong.

flags: minor: context (first offense small fine, repeated offenses heavier) defines the word right after the colon, so the item is very easy; D ('same for everyone') is the one plausible trap
R030-04.notes: Penalties rise with repeated offenses, so they increase in steps.

flags: minor: lookup cue - A closely paraphrases 'outsiders could not watch every field and canal'
R030-05.notes: Para 5 gives two reasons: outsiders could not watch, and users with no say had less reason to respect rules. A matches the first.

R030-06.notes: The examples are real commons that lasted under rules users enforced. A overclaims ('every'), which para 4 rejects; C reverses the purpose; B is unsupported.

flags: minor: lookup cue - A closely paraphrases 'he had described one possible ending as if it were the only one'
minor: overlaps with R030-01 and R030-08 on the same final-paragraph idea
R030-07.notes: Final paragraph: Ostrom did not prove Hardin wrong but showed he treated one ending as the only one. B overstates, since many cases collapsed.

R030-08.notes: Hardin's herders cannot talk or make agreements. Ostrom's herders can, which is how they set and enforce rules. A and D are explicitly in Hardin's model; C is not about communication.

flags: minor: C maps almost one-to-one onto the para 4 list (a voice in changing rules, mutual monitoring, graduated penalties), so it is easy to spot; each distractor breaks an obvious principle
R030-09.notes: This applies Ostrom's design principles to a new case. A is a distant authority with weak monitoring, B is open access with no monitoring, and D is privatization.

flags: minor: para 6 says 'some voices that had thrived in front of the horn sounded harsh or thin up close', which makes B a mild reverse trap, though a sound one
R030-10.notes: Para 3: gentle-voiced singers had to project. Para 6: a microphone could catch a quiet voice. C is unaffected, since the time limit was a disc constraint. D describes a horn-era technique.
